passage: The recruiter's office in Toronto smelled of coffee and new carpet. Clara slid the offer across the desk. "We have many candidates for this role," she said. "If you can sign today, it's yours." Kaito's stomach tightened. He liked the job, and he could hear the clock. But he noticed how quickly the line had arrived, before he had read a single page. "Could you email me the terms in writing? I would like to read them tonight and reply tomorrow morning." Clara's smile thinned. "I can't hold it for long." "Understood," Kaito said, pleasantly. "Tomorrow by ten." On the train home he felt shaky, but also strangely calm, as if he had put one foot back on the ground. The email came an hour later.

qa.q: In which city was the recruiter's office?
qa.a: The recruiter's office was in Toronto.

qa.q: Why did Kaito's stomach tighten when Clara told him to sign today?
qa.a: He felt rushed and pressured, because he liked the job but was being asked to decide before reading any pages.

qa.q: What could Kaito do when the written terms arrive?
qa.a: He can read them carefully that evening, note any questions, and reply the next morning, knowing a real offer should survive a day.

qa.q: How might Clara have seen Kaito's request?
qa.a: Clara's smile thinned, so she may have felt pushed against her plan, or worried about other candidates. A real recruiter can still accept a reasonable request for time.

grounding: A recruiter says 'we have many candidates, sign today'; the protagonist feels rushed and asks for the terms in writing and time to decide.
